chapter_summary: Proverbs 23 gives wisdom for everyday life — eating with powerful people, working hard without greed, honouring your parents, guarding your heart, and avoiding the trap of wine. At its centre is a call to seek truth and wisdom above every other treasure. The chapter warns that riches fly away like birds, that those who live for the wrong things end up broken and lost, and that a child who grows in wisdom brings the greatest joy a parent can know. God's wisdom protects; foolish paths lead to ruin.
main_lesson: Choose wisdom and truth over greed, wine, and the wrong path — they lead to ruin. Wisdom and a pure heart bring lasting joy.

memory_verse.kjv: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
memory_verse.little_bible: Get the truth and never let it go. Hold on to wisdom. Hold on to what is right.

parent_guide: Proverbs 23 is one of the richest and most varied chapters in the book. It covers table manners and humility before the powerful (vv. 1-3), the danger of striving for wealth (vv. 4-5), false generosity (vv. 6-8), futile speech to fools (v. 9), care for the vulnerable (vv. 10-11), the role of discipline and instruction (vv. 12-14), the joy a wise child brings to a parent's heart (vv. 15-16), trust in God rather than envy of sinners (vv. 17-18), sobriety and self-control (vv. 19-21), honouring parents (v. 22), the supremacy of truth (v. 23), parental joy (vv. 24-25), the father's appeal (v. 26), warning about sexual immorality (vv. 27-28), and a vivid extended warning against drunkenness (vv. 29-35). The chapter holds together practical wisdom, relational wisdom, and deep moral warnings in a single urgent voice. For children, the most accessible themes are: truth is worth more than anything, parents love a wise child, and some paths look good but lead to great harm. The warnings about wine in verses 29-35 are among the most graphic in Proverbs — the vivid imagery of snakebite, stumbling at sea, and the drinker's confession ('I felt nothing') is designed to shock the reader into awareness. Use this as an opportunity to talk about why some things that look appealing can cause very real harm.
application_for_children: This week, hold on to one true thing from God's Word. Say it every morning. When something tempting comes up, ask yourself: 'Will this help me grow in wisdom, or pull me away from it?'

verses.kjv: When thou sittest to eat with a ruler, consider diligently what is before thee:
verses.little_bible: When you sit to eat with someone important, think carefully. Look at what is in front of you. Be wise at the table.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Be wise and careful when eating with important people.
verses.meaning: This verse counsels humility and thoughtfulness in the presence of the powerful. The banquet table of a ruler is not the place for carelessness or appetite-driven behaviour. Wisdom requires reading the situation and governing yourself accordingly.
verses.prayer: God, help me think carefully in every situation.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we be careful and thoughtful around important people?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to read a room — to understand that different situations call for different kinds of behaviour and self-discipline?
verses.do_it_today: At your next meal, sit down, look at what is in front of you, and say a thoughtful thank-you before eating.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting at a grand table with an important-looking adult, pausing thoughtfully before eating, a warm candlelit room, watercolour style

verses.kjv: And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite.
verses.little_bible: If you always want more food, stop yourself. Your hunger should not control you. You must be in charge of what you want.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not let your appetite control you — be in charge of yourself.
verses.meaning: This is an extreme, vivid way of saying: if you are prone to greed and overindulgence, take drastic self-control. The imagery is deliberately shocking — discipline yourself before your appetite gets you into trouble, especially in the company of the powerful.
verses.prayer: God, help me not let hunger or greed control me.
verses.discussion_question: How do you stop yourself when you want too much of something?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help children develop self-control over appetite — whether for food, screen time, or possessions — not through shame but through wisdom and practice?
verses.do_it_today: When you feel like asking for more than you need today, pause and choose to be content with enough.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child at a table, hand raised to pause, thoughtfully choosing to stop rather than grab more food, calm self-control on their face, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Be not desirous of his dainties: for they are deceitful meat.
verses.little_bible: Do not want the special food of a powerful person. It may look wonderful. But it is a trap — it is not what it seems.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not be fooled by fine food — it can be a trap.
verses.meaning: The rich food on a ruler's table may come with hidden strings — obligation, flattery, or the expectation of a favour. Wisdom sees through the surface appeal to the true cost beneath. Not everything that looks good is freely given.
verses.prayer: God, help me see past what things look like.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever wanted something that looked good but was actually bad for you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children to think beyond the surface — to ask 'what is the cost of this?' before reaching for what looks appealing?
verses.do_it_today: Before you reach for something today, ask: 'Is this really as good as it looks?' Think before you grab.
verses.illustration_prompt: A plate of beautiful, colourful food with a subtle shadow of a trap beneath it, a wise child pulling back their hand, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Labour not to be rich: cease from thine own wisdom.
verses.little_bible: Do not wear yourself out trying to get rich. Stop trusting only in your own clever ideas. That is not wisdom.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not wear yourself out chasing riches — trust God, not your own plans.
verses.meaning: Proverbs is not opposed to work or wealth, but to making wealth the goal of all effort. 'Cease from thine own wisdom' means: stop trusting your own understanding as the ultimate guide. True wisdom surrenders the pursuit of riches to God's priorities.
verses.prayer: God, help me not chase money more than I chase You.
verses.discussion_question: What is something better to work hard for than just getting rich?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model for our children a right relationship with work and wealth — diligent but not driven, productive but not greedy?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing you are working for. Is it money, or is it something that truly matters? Refocus if needed.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child running after a bag of gold that keeps moving further away, looking tired and sad, while another child rests in green grass under God's light, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: Wilt thou set thine eyes upon that which is not? for riches certainly make themselves wings; they fly away as an eagle toward heaven.
verses.little_bible: Why do you stare at riches? They are not really yours to keep. Riches grow wings and fly away. They go like an eagle to the sky.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Riches fly away like an eagle — do not put your heart in them.
verses.meaning: Riches are fleeting — they have a tendency to vanish. The image of wealth sprouting wings and flying away like an eagle is one of the most memorable in Proverbs. The verse warns against staking life, hope, or security on something so unstable.
verses.prayer: God, keep my heart from chasing what flies away.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it a bad idea to put all your hope in money?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the difference between lasting treasure — character, faith, relationships — and fleeting wealth?
verses.do_it_today: Name one thing that will last forever. Name one that will not. Which one are you chasing most?
verses.illustration_prompt: Gold coins sprouting eagle wings and soaring away into the sky, a child watching with open empty hands, learning not to cling to riches, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Eat thou not the bread of him that hath an evil eye, neither desire thou his dainty meats:
verses.little_bible: Do not eat the food of a stingy, mean person. Do not want his special things. His eye is evil. He is not truly giving.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not eat the food of a mean, stingy person — it is not truly given.
verses.meaning: The 'evil eye' in Hebrew idiom refers to a miserly, selfish person. What looks like generosity from such a person is not real — it comes with resentment or a hidden price. Wisdom recognises false generosity and refuses to be drawn in by it.
verses.prayer: God, help me see when kindness is not real.
verses.discussion_question: How can you tell if someone is truly being kind or just pretending?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children to give generously and to be alert to the difference between genuine and manipulative giving?
verses.do_it_today: Give something to someone today with no strings attached — a true, free gift. Notice how that feels.
verses.illustration_prompt: A person offering food with a forced smile and suspicious shadowed eyes, a wise child stepping back politely, watercolour style

verses.kjv: For as he thinketh in his heart, so is he: Eat and drink, saith he to thee; but his heart is not with thee.
verses.little_bible: What a person thinks inside is who they really are. He says: eat, drink! But his heart is not truly with you. His words are not honest.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: What is in your heart is who you really are.
verses.meaning: This verse contains one of the great wisdom truths: the heart reveals the true person. Outward words of welcome can mask an inward reluctance or resentment. The 'eat and drink' invitation is hollow because the host's heart is not in it. What we think in our hearts shapes who we are.
verses.memory_phrase: Your heart is who you are.
verses.prayer: God, keep my heart honest and truly kind.
verses.discussion_question: Why does what we think in our hearts matter more than what we say with our mouths?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate inward integrity in our children — helping them care as much about what they think as about what they say or do?
verses.do_it_today: Think about one thing you said today. Did your heart match your words? If not, why not?
verses.illustration_prompt: A person with a smiling face and welcoming hand but a dark closed heart inside their chest, contrasted with a child whose face and heart are the same warm light, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: The morsel which thou hast eaten shalt thou vomit up, and lose thy sweet words.
verses.little_bible: The food you eat there will make you feel sick inside. And all your kind words will be wasted. Nothing good will come from it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Eating from a false friend brings regret and wasted words.
verses.meaning: The consequence of accepting false hospitality is both physical and relational disgust — you will regret having eaten and all the pleasant words exchanged will be exposed as meaningless. The wise person avoids relationships built on pretence.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose honest friends over false ones.
verses.discussion_question: Have you ever done something with someone and later felt it was wrong? What did you learn?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children discern true friendships from those that look good on the surface but lead to regret?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a friendship. Is it honest and real? If not, what small step can you take toward more honest friendship?
verses.illustration_prompt: A child looking sad and sorry after eating at a false friend's table, wasted kind words floating away like smoke, a lesson learned, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Speak not in the ears of a fool: for he will despise the wisdom of thy words.
verses.little_bible: Do not share wisdom with someone who hates it. A foolish person will just really hate your wise words. Your wisdom will be wasted on them.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not waste wise words on someone who hates wisdom.
verses.meaning: Wisdom must be offered discerningly. The fool — not merely someone unlearned, but someone who actively rejects wisdom — will treat good counsel with contempt. There is a time for speaking and a time for staying silent, and wasting wisdom on an unwilling heart is itself unwise.
verses.prayer: God, give me wisdom to know when to speak.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it sometimes right to stay quiet instead of giving advice?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach children the wisdom of choosing their audience — not withholding truth, but recognising when a heart is ready to receive it?
verses.do_it_today: Before sharing advice today, ask: 'Is this person ready to hear this? Will it help?' If not, pray instead of speaking.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child offering a glowing scroll of wisdom to another who turns away and scowls, the wise child learning to step back with quiet dignity, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Remove not the old landmark; and enter not into the fields of the fatherless:
verses.little_bible: Do not move the boundary stones that belong to someone else. Do not take land from children who have no father. That is very wrong.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not steal from those who have no one to protect them.
verses.meaning: Boundary stones marked property lines in ancient Israel. Moving them was a form of theft — a way of taking land from someone who depended on it for survival. The fatherless had no legal protector, making them especially vulnerable to this kind of exploitation. God takes this seriously.
verses.prayer: God, help me never take from those who have less.
verses.discussion_question: Who are the people in our world who need protecting most? How can we help them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate in our children a protective heart toward the vulnerable — those without parents, resources, or advocates?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one person in your life who needs protecting or supporting. Do one small thing to help them today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child standing bravely in front of a boundary stone, protecting it and the small children behind it, warm determined expression, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For their redeemer is mighty; he shall plead their cause with thee.
verses.little_bible: The one who fights for them is mighty. God is on their side. He will stand up for them against you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: God is the mighty defender of those with no one else.
verses.meaning: The 'redeemer' here is the go'el — the kinsman-redeemer, the protector of the family. The fatherless child's redeemer is God Himself. He is mighty and will plead their cause. This is a strong deterrent: whoever wrongs the vulnerable will face God as their opponent.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for defending those who have no one.
verses.discussion_question: How does it feel to know God stands up for people who are alone and helpless?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that God is the defender of the weak — and that we are called to partner with Him in that work?
verses.do_it_today: Pray today for one person who has no one to stand up for them. Ask God to defend and protect them.
verses.illustration_prompt: A mighty shining figure standing protectively over a small child who has no parents, God's presence strong and comforting, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Apply thine heart unto instruction, and thine ears to the words of knowledge.
verses.little_bible: Give your heart to learning. Open your ears to words of knowledge. Let what you hear go deep inside you.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Give your whole heart and both ears to learning.
verses.meaning: Instruction must be received at the heart level, not just heard at the surface. 'Apply your heart' is an active commitment — a deliberate turning of the will and affections toward wisdom. Both heart and ears must be engaged for real learning to happen.
verses.prayer: God, help me listen with my whole heart.
verses.discussion_question: What is the difference between just hearing something and really taking it into your heart?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children move from hearing instruction to truly applying it at the heart level — internalising rather than just complying?
verses.do_it_today: Read or listen to one wise thing today. Then ask yourself: 'What is my heart going to do with this?'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child with their hand on their heart, listening with bright open ears as words of wisdom gently flow in and take root in their heart, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Withhold not correction from the child: for if thou beatest him with the rod, he shall not die.
verses.little_bible: Do not hold back correction from a child. Discipline helps them. It will not destroy them — it will help them grow.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not hold back right correction from a child — it helps them grow.
verses.meaning: This verse is addressed to parents and teachers. It commands that correction not be withheld — the child will not be ruined by discipline, but by its absence. The rod is the instrument of loving, purposeful correction, not cruelty. Withholding correction is itself a form of harm.
verses.prayer: God, help me receive correction and learn from it.
verses.discussion_question: Why does being corrected actually help a child become better?
verses.family_discussion: How do we practise loving, purposeful correction in our family — neither withholding it nor applying it without wisdom and love?
verses.do_it_today: When you receive correction today, say thank you for it. Choose to grow from it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A parent gently but firmly guiding a small child back to the right path, the child looking up with trust, both in warm golden light, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Thou shalt beat him with the rod, and shalt deliver his soul from hell.
verses.little_bible: Loving discipline saves a child. It keeps them from the wrong path. Correction now protects their whole life.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Loving correction saves a child from a life of ruin.
verses.meaning: The goal of discipline is not punishment — it is salvation from a far worse outcome. 'Sheol' here points to destruction, ruin, and death as the ultimate fruit of undisciplined living. Correcting a child now is an act of profound love that delivers them from future ruin.
verses.prayer: God, thank You for those who love me enough to correct me.
verses.discussion_question: How is correcting a child an act of love, not cruelty?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that the corrections they receive are acts of love — that the goal is always their flourishing, not punishment for its own sake?
verses.do_it_today: Thank someone who has ever corrected or disciplined you in love. Let them know it helped you.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child being guided away from a dark dangerous road by a loving parent onto a bright safe path, warmth and protection in the scene, watercolour style

verses.kjv: My son, if thine heart be wise, my heart shall rejoice, even mine.
verses.little_bible: My child, if your heart grows in wisdom, my heart will be so glad! Your wisdom fills my heart with joy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A wise child fills their parent's heart with joy.
verses.meaning: The parent's joy is personal and deep — 'even mine' emphasises that this is not a formal obligation but a heartfelt response. Wisdom in a child does something to the parent that nothing else can do. This is one of the most tender verses in Proverbs.
verses.prayer: God, help me grow in wisdom and make my parents glad.
verses.discussion_question: How does it make your parents feel when you make wise and good choices?
verses.family_discussion: How do we communicate the depth of our joy when our children make wise choices — not just correcting the wrong, but celebrating the right?
verses.do_it_today: Tell your child one wise thing you saw them do recently and how much joy it gave you. Be specific.
verses.illustration_prompt: A parent and child face to face, both glowing with joy, the parent's eyes full of proud love as the child makes a wise choice, warm watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Yea, my reins shall rejoice, when thy lips speak right things.
verses.little_bible: My whole inner self will jump for joy. When your lips speak what is right and true, I am overjoyed inside.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: When you speak right things, your parents rejoice deep inside.
verses.meaning: 'My reins' refers to the deepest inner being — the seat of emotion and thought. When a child speaks what is right, the parent's joy is not surface-level but goes to the deepest place. True speech produces deep joy in those who love us.
verses.memory_phrase: Speak what is right and true.
verses.prayer: God, help my words be right and bring joy.
verses.discussion_question: What are some right and true things you can say that would make someone you love very happy?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build a family culture where speaking truth and right things is celebrated — where our children feel the joy of honest, good speech?
verses.do_it_today: Say one true and right thing today to someone you love. Watch what happens to their face.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child speaking clearly and honestly with warm words of truth flowing out, a parent nearby glowing with deep inner joy, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Let not thine heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the LORD all the day long.
verses.little_bible: Do not want what people who do wrong have. Instead, honour and respect God every single day. That is the better way.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not envy wrongdoers — honour God all day long instead.
verses.meaning: Envy of sinners is a recurring danger addressed in Proverbs and Psalms (see Psalm 73). The answer is not to work harder or acquire more — it is to maintain the fear of the Lord as the constant frame of life. Envy of the wicked flows from losing sight of God.
verses.prayer: God, help me honour You all day and not envy wrong people.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we not want what people who do wrong have, even if it looks good?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children resist the envy of those who seem to prosper through wrong — keeping their eyes fixed on God's value system rather than the world's?
verses.do_it_today: When you notice envy rising today, say: 'God is better. His way is better.' Then choose to honour Him in that moment.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child turning away from something glittering but shadowed, and instead looking up with peace and reverence toward God's warm light, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For surely there is an end; and thine expectation shall not be cut off.
verses.little_bible: There is always an end to every story. Keep trusting God. Your hope will not be cut off. God's way leads to the best ending.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Keep hoping in God — your hope will not be cut off.
verses.meaning: This verse reassures the believer: the wicked may prosper now, but there is an end. The believer's hope and expectation — rooted in God — will not be cut off. This is the ground for resisting envy: the final story has not yet been told, and it ends well for those who trust God.
verses.prayer: God, I trust You with my future. My hope is in You.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it good to know that God controls how every story ends?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build in our children an eschatological hope — the conviction that God's story ends rightly and that trusting Him is never wasted?
verses.do_it_today: Write down one thing you are hoping for. Pray: 'God, I trust You. My hope is in You, not in anything else.'
verses.illustration_prompt: A child looking toward a distant bright horizon with calm hope, a long road ahead but God's light shining at the end of it, peaceful watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Hear thou, my son, and be wise, and guide thine heart in the way.
verses.little_bible: Listen, my child. Be wise. Guide your heart on the right way. You must lead your own heart well.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Listen, be wise, and guide your own heart in the right way.
verses.meaning: Wisdom requires active self-governance. 'Guide your heart in the way' means taking responsibility for your own inner life — not being led by every impulse or feeling, but directing your heart with intentionality along God's path.
verses.prayer: God, help me lead my heart on the right path.
verses.discussion_question: How do you guide your heart when it wants to go the wrong way?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children learn self-governance — the practice of steering their own hearts toward what is right rather than being carried by feelings or impulses?
verses.do_it_today: When your heart pulls you toward something wrong today, pause and guide it back. You are in charge of your heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding their own heart like a compass, steering it deliberately onto a bright right path, calm and purposeful expression, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Be not among winebibbers; among riotous eaters of flesh:
verses.little_bible: Do not spend time with people who drink too much. Do not be with those who eat wildly without control. Stay away from that crowd.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Stay away from people who drink too much and live without control.
verses.meaning: The warning is about company and lifestyle. Those who over-drink and over-indulge in every appetite create an environment that pulls others toward the same pattern. Wisdom is partly about choosing who you spend time with.
verses.prayer: God, help me choose friends who help me do right.
verses.discussion_question: Why does it matter who we spend our time with?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand that the company they keep shapes who they become — and how do we guide them toward good friendships?
verses.do_it_today: Think about the people you spend the most time with. Do they help you grow wiser? If not, what can you do?
verses.illustration_prompt: A child stepping away from a rowdy out-of-control group and walking toward a calm, wise group of friends, quiet determination in their step, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For the drunkard and the glutton shall come to poverty: and drowsiness shall clothe a man with rags.
verses.little_bible: The person who drinks too much and eats without control will end up with nothing. Laziness and no self-control will leave them in rags.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: No self-control leads to poverty and rags.
verses.meaning: Self-indulgence has a cost. Over-drinking and over-eating without restraint leads to poverty — both material and spiritual. Drowsiness (lack of alertness, laziness) is both a cause and a symbol of this kind of decline. The fruit of no self-control is loss.
verses.prayer: God, help me have self-control so I do not lose what matters.
verses.discussion_question: What can happen when people have no self-control over what they eat or drink?
verses.family_discussion: How do we cultivate genuine self-control in our children — not just as a rule to follow, but as a wisdom practice that protects their future?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one area of life today where you will practise self-control. Start small. Build the habit.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure in ragged clothes, slumped and tired, as a result of no self-control, contrasted with a wise self-controlled child who is healthy and cared-for, watercolour comparison

verses.kjv: Hearken unto thy father that begat thee, and despise not thy mother when she is old.
verses.little_bible: Listen to your father. He is the one who raised you. Do not reject your mother when she is old. Honour them both.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Listen to your father and honour your mother always.
verses.meaning: This verse gives a direct command: listen to your father and do not despise your mother in old age. The connection between who begat you and who you should listen to is direct — parents are owed honour across every season of life, including when they are aged and perhaps less impressive to the world.
verses.prayer: God, help me truly listen to and honour my parents.
verses.discussion_question: What is one way you can show your parents that you really listen to them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we model honouring our own parents in front of our children — giving them a vision of what honouring aged parents looks like?
verses.do_it_today: Do one thing today that shows your parents you truly hear and honour them. Make it specific and sincere.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child sitting close and listening attentively to their father, an older grandmother nearby being gently honoured, warm family scene, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Buy the truth, and sell it not; also wisdom, and instruction, and understanding.
verses.little_bible: Get the truth. Pay any price for it. Never let it go. Hold on to wisdom. Hold on to what is right.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Get the truth and never give it up — it is worth everything.
verses.meaning: Truth is presented as the supreme acquisition — something worth paying any price to obtain and refusing any price to surrender. 'Buy' does not mean money — it means: spend whatever it costs. Truth, wisdom, instruction, and understanding are four facets of the same treasure. To sell truth is to lose the very foundation of a wise life.
verses.prayer: God, help me hold on to truth and never give it up.
verses.discussion_question: Why should we never trade away the truth — even if something else looks better?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop a love of truth — not just an obligation to honesty, but a deep desire to know, hold, and live by what is true?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one truth from God's Word you know. Say it out loud three times. Decide you will never trade it away.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding a glowing scroll of truth with both hands, refusing to let go, light pouring from it, warmth and determination on their face, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: The father of the righteous shall greatly rejoice: and he that begetteth a wise child shall have joy of him.
verses.little_bible: A father whose child does right is filled with great joy. A parent who raises a wise child — that child is their greatest joy.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: A righteous, wise child brings a father's greatest joy.
verses.meaning: This verse continues the parent-child joy theme from verses 15-16. A righteous and wise child is a source of the deepest parental joy. This frames the whole chapter's appeal: the father is not commanding out of power but appealing out of love, longing to rejoice over the child's flourishing.
verses.prayer: God, help me be a child who brings joy to my family.
verses.discussion_question: What is the best gift you can give your parents — not bought, but lived?
verses.family_discussion: How do we communicate to our children that their character and wisdom — not their achievements or talents — are our greatest source of joy?
verses.do_it_today: Tell your parent or carer one way you are trying to grow in wisdom. Let them share in it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A father laughing with deep open joy, arms around a child who has clearly made a wise and righteous choice, pure happiness in the scene, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Thy father and thy mother shall be glad, and she that bare thee shall rejoice.
verses.little_bible: Your father and your mother will be glad. The mother who gave birth to you will rejoice. Your wisdom is their great happiness.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Your wisdom makes both your parents truly glad.
verses.meaning: Both parents are mentioned here — father and mother share equally in the joy of a wise child. The specific mention of 'she who bore you' (your mother) adds tenderness. The pain of birth is answered by the joy of the child's righteous life.
verses.prayer: God, help me grow so my parents can rejoice.
verses.discussion_question: How does it feel when someone you love is truly happy because of you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we let our children know — in words and in showing it — how much their wisdom and goodness delight us?
verses.do_it_today: Do one wise, right thing today and tell your parent you did it and why. Watch their face.
verses.illustration_prompt: A mother and father both smiling and glowing with pride and joy, their child standing between them looking up with love, warm golden family scene, watercolour style

verses.kjv: My son, give me thine heart, and let thine eyes observe my ways.
verses.little_bible: My child, give me your heart. Watch my ways. Follow how I walk. Let your heart be fully with me.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Give your heart to wisdom and watch the right path.
verses.meaning: This is perhaps the most tender appeal in the chapter — a father asking not for outward compliance but for the child's heart. Combined with 'let your eyes observe my ways,' it is an invitation to the deepest form of discipleship: watch closely, give your heart, follow the path.
verses.prayer: God, I give You my heart. I want to follow You.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to give your heart to someone you trust?
verses.family_discussion: How do we as parents live in a way that our children want to watch and follow — modelling the ways of wisdom so clearly that our children's eyes are drawn to them?
verses.do_it_today: Tell God today: 'I give You my heart.' Then write down one way you will follow His path today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child holding out their heart with open hands toward a loving father figure who represents wisdom, eyes watching and ready to follow, beautiful tender watercolour scene

verses.kjv: For a whore is a deep ditch; and a strange woman is a narrow pit.
verses.little_bible: The wrong path leads to a very deep trap. It catches those who fall into it. It is very hard to get out. Stay away from it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wrong path is a deep trap — stay far away.
verses.meaning: This verse is part of the father's urgent warning about sexual immorality. The imagery of a deep ditch and narrow pit conveys entrapment — once you fall in, it is extremely difficult to get out. The warning is not against all women but against the pattern of sinful sexual behaviour, which Scripture consistently presents as a deadly trap.
verses.memory_phrase: Stay away from the wrong path.
verses.prayer: God, keep me far from every trap and wrong path.
verses.discussion_question: What should you do when you see a path that looks easy but leads somewhere dangerous?
verses.family_discussion: How do we give our children a healthy, biblically-grounded understanding of God's design for relationships — so they understand why this warning exists and what they are being protected from?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one thing that looks inviting but could be a trap. Decide now to stay away from it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child stopping at the edge of a deep dark pit hidden under beautiful flowers, choosing to step back onto the safe bright path, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: She also lieth in wait as for a prey, and increaseth the transgressors among men.
verses.little_bible: This wrong path waits like a hunter for those who do not see the danger. More and more people fall into sin this way. Be alert.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wrong path hunts for those who are not alert — stay alert.
verses.meaning: The image shifts to a predator lying in wait — the danger is active, not passive. It hunts. And it multiplies sinners — those who fall into this pattern draw others in with them. The warning is both personal and social: this path destroys individuals and communities.
verses.prayer: God, make me alert. Help me see danger before I fall.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to see a danger before you get too close to it?
verses.family_discussion: How do we build alertness and discernment in our children — the ability to recognise danger early and respond before it is too late?
verses.do_it_today: When something feels slightly wrong today, pay attention to that feeling. Do not ignore it. Ask God for wisdom.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child walking a path with a warning lamp held high, alert eyes spotting a hidden danger ahead in time to step away safely, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Who hath woe? who hath sorrow? who hath contentions? who hath babbling? who hath wounds without cause? who hath redness of eyes?
verses.little_bible: Who has trouble? Who has sorrow? Who fights with everyone? Who is always confused? Who gets hurt for no reason? Who has sore, red eyes?
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Who has nothing but trouble, sorrow, and pain?
verses.meaning: This powerful sequence of six questions builds a portrait of the consequences of excessive drinking. The accumulation — woe, sorrow, quarrels, complaints, wounds, red eyes — is deliberately overwhelming. The poet is naming the full wreckage of a life controlled by wine. The answer to all six questions comes in verse 30.
verses.prayer: God, protect me from choices that bring woe and pain.
verses.discussion_question: If you saw someone with all these troubles, what kind of choices do you think they might have made?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children connect the dots between present choices and future consequences — seeing that today's decisions shape tomorrow's condition?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one choice you made recently. What might it lead to? Is it leading toward life or toward trouble?
verses.illustration_prompt: Six small sad pictures side by side — trouble, sorrow, fights, confusion, wounds, red eyes — the portrait of a life of bad choices, expressive watercolour style

verses.kjv: They that tarry long at the wine; they that go to seek mixed wine.
verses.little_bible: These troubles come to those who stay too long drinking wine. They keep going back for more. That is who ends up this way.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Those who drink and keep drinking end up with all that trouble.
verses.meaning: The answer to the six questions of verse 29: it is those who linger over wine, who go looking for more, who choose to stay in the place of excess rather than leave. The disaster is not accidental — it is the fruit of deliberate, repeated choices to stay and indulge.
verses.prayer: God, help me not go back to things that hurt me.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it dangerous to keep going back to something that hurts you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the danger of repeated bad choices — how habits form and how they become hard to break?
verses.do_it_today: Think of one habit you have. Is it helping you or hurting you? Talk to someone you trust about it.
verses.illustration_prompt: A figure returning again and again to a cup that brings harm, footprints in a circle showing the repeating pattern, a sad scene of being trapped, watercolour style

verses.kjv: Look not thou upon the wine when it is red, when it giveth his colour in the cup, when it moveth itself aright.
verses.little_bible: Do not even look at the wine when it looks beautiful in the cup. Do not let its beauty pull you in. The danger is real.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: Do not let the beauty of something dangerous draw you in.
verses.meaning: The warning is to stop at the point of looking — before drinking, before even being drawn in by the appeal. The wine is described as beautiful and attractive. That is part of the danger. Wisdom begins at the point of not looking, not just at the point of not drinking.
verses.memory_phrase: Do not look at what pulls you wrong.
verses.prayer: God, help me look away from things that will lead me wrong.
verses.discussion_question: Why is the very first look at something dangerous already a risk?
verses.family_discussion: How do we teach our children to identify the entry points of temptation — not just the action itself, but the moment of looking, longing, and entertaining?
verses.do_it_today: When you notice something tempting today, look away quickly. Do not let it draw you in. Practise this.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child deliberately turning their eyes away from a shining but dangerous cup, choosing not to even look, wisdom and strength on their face, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: At the last it biteth like a serpent, and stingeth like an adder.
verses.little_bible: In the end, it bites like a snake. It stings like a deadly serpent. What looked beautiful causes great harm in the end.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: What looks good at first bites like a snake in the end.
verses.meaning: The delayed bite of the serpent is a brilliant image for the danger of wine: its harm is not immediate, which makes it deceptive. Like a snake, it strikes when you are not expecting it. The consequence is real, sharp, and painful — not something that can be easily undone.
verses.prayer: God, help me see what beautiful traps will do in the end.
verses.discussion_question: Have you heard of something that looked good but bit people in the end? What should we remember?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop long-term thinking — weighing what something costs at the end, not just what it offers at the beginning?
verses.do_it_today: Think of a choice you are facing. Think about what it looks like right now — and then think about what it might look like a year from now.
verses.illustration_prompt: A beautiful golden cup transforming into a striking serpent at the moment of drinking, the hidden danger revealed, powerful and dramatic watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Thine eyes shall behold strange women, and thine heart shall utter perverse things.
verses.little_bible: Your eyes will see wrong things. Your heart will think and say things that are twisted and bad. This is where that path leads.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wrong path leads to wrong seeing and wrong thinking.
verses.meaning: The effects of drunkenness extend beyond physical harm — they corrupt perception and the inner life. The eyes see wrongly; the heart produces corrupted thoughts and words. What we feed our minds and senses shapes what we see and say. The degradation of the inner person is the deepest harm.
verses.prayer: God, guard my eyes and keep my heart from twisted thinking.
verses.discussion_question: Why is it important to guard what your eyes look at?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children understand the connection between what they feed their minds and what their hearts produce — in words, thoughts, and desires?
verses.do_it_today: Choose one thing today to keep your eyes away from that you know is not good for your heart.
verses.illustration_prompt: A child shielding their eyes from dark confusing images, turning instead toward clear and clean light, a protective and wise gesture, watercolour scene

verses.kjv: Yea, thou shalt be as he that lieth down in the midst of the sea, or as he that lieth upon the top of a mast.
verses.little_bible: You will be like someone sleeping in the middle of a wild sea. Or someone lying on top of a tall ship mast. You will be in great danger and not even know it.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The wrong path leaves you in great danger without knowing it.
verses.meaning: The images are vivid and terrifying: lying in the sea's midst is to be in mortal danger without solid ground; lying on top of a mast is to be in danger of falling at any moment. The drunkard is oblivious to their extreme vulnerability. This is among the most dramatic consequence descriptions in all of Proverbs.
verses.memory_phrase: Sin leaves you in real danger.
verses.prayer: God, keep me from danger I cannot see. Open my eyes.
verses.discussion_question: What does it mean to be in danger without even knowing it? How can wisdom protect you?
verses.family_discussion: How do we help our children develop spiritual alertness — an awareness of dangers they cannot always immediately see?
verses.do_it_today: Ask God today to show you any danger in your life you may not be seeing. Be still and listen.
verses.illustration_prompt: A small figure clinging to a ship mast in a stormy sea, eyes closed and unaware of how dangerous their position is, the storm raging around them, dramatic watercolour scene

verses.kjv: They have stricken me, shalt thou say, and I was not sick; they have beaten me, and I felt it not: when shall I awake? I will seek it yet again.
verses.little_bible: The person says: They hit me and I did not feel it. They hurt me and I did not notice. When I wake up, I will go and do it all again. This is a terrible trap.
verses.little_reader_adaptation: The person is so trapped they do not even notice the harm — and they go back for more.
verses.meaning: This is the darkest verse of the chapter — the voice of the addicted person who has lost the ability to feel pain, learn from consequences, and choose differently. The tragic final line — 'I will seek it yet again' — shows the full grip of the trap. It is a mercy-less portrait of what the path of no self-control leads to, and it stands as the chapter's final warning.
verses.memory_phrase: The worst trap is the one you choose.
verses.prayer: God, save me from traps I cannot see or feel. Set me free.
verses.discussion_question: What is sad about this person? Why should we feel sorry for them — and learn from them?
verses.family_discussion: How do we create a family environment where children feel safe to name a bad habit or a trap they are in — and know they will receive help, not shame?
verses.do_it_today: If you are trapped by anything — a habit, a feeling, a choice you keep making — tell God. Ask for His help to get free today.
verses.illustration_prompt: A weary figure waking up hurt and confused, but immediately turning back toward the same dangerous thing, the sadness of the trap clear, a call to break free, watercolour scene
